title: Adaptive rerank parallelism and deadline-aware batching for lower tail latency
creator: Marina Ortiz
description: Goal: Reduce 99th-percentile latency for the reranking endpoint under mixed workloads by combining adaptive request parallelism with deadline-aware batching and per-request token caps. This ticket designs and implements a runtime layer that dynamically shards long candidate lists, enforces soft token limits per request, and uses deadline-driven batch flushing to prioritize low-latency requests without starving high-throughput customers.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for rerank endpoint decreases by >=20% on synthetic mixed workload (short chat-like requests + long document reranks)
No functional change to ranking scores for requests under token limit; degradation for requests that hit soft cap must be predictable and documented
System supports configurable per-customer soft token cap and deadline window in console
New metrics and dashboards capture shard-level latency, dropped-token events, and deadline-triggered flushes
implementation_notes: Introduce a sharding policy that splits candidate lists into N shards where N = min(max_shards, ceil(len(candidates)/shard_size_hint))
Add a scheduler that issues parallel scoring RPCs to worker executors with backpressure awareness (tokens-in-flight limit per-worker)
Implement soft_token_cap per-request: if total tokens > cap, score top-K prefixes and mark 'soft_capped' in response metadata
Deadline-aware batching: each batch has a cumulative wall-clock deadline; when first request approaches deadline_threshold, flush partial batch to avoid tail latency
Fallback path: if shards fail or timeout, fall back to single-threaded scoring of first M candidates to produce partial response
Expose console controls: default soft cap = 2048 tokens, shard_size_hint = 128 candidates, deadline_threshold = 12ms before SLA deadline
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Parallel shards improve throughput but increase peak GPU memory/KV cache pressure — mitigated by adaptive max_shards tied to observed GPU free memory
Soft token caps favor latency but can reduce quality for long-context reranks; plan to add per-customer override and an evaluation suite to quantify quality loss
Deadline-driven flush reduces tail but may increase average compute due to partial work; acceptable under latency-first SLOs for supported tiers
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: RFC submitted outlining sharding + deadline batching approach. Reviewed by Liam Chen and Aisha Kapoor — consensus to prototype in worker executor layer.
2026-03-11: Prototype implemented in a feature branch (github.com/redwood/repro/rerank-deadline-proto). Basic sharding with parallel RPCs wired to executor; simple deadline timer added.

2026-03-12: Load test results on staging: mixed workload (70% short, 30% long) shows P99 down 18% with shard_size_hint 128 and max_shards 4. Observed 12% increase in GPU memory pressure for peak windows.
2026-03-13: Design review with runtime team. Agreed to add per-worker in-flight token cap and implement soft-token metadata in responses. Assigned follow-ups for metrics and console UI.
Next: Add fair-share batching to avoid noisy tenants consuming shards, add unit + e2e tests, and run extended soak tests
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Memory pressure and higher OOM risk on large models when parallel shards overlap KV cache usage. Mitigation: adaptive max_shards based on free GPU memory and eviction policies for shard KV caches.
Risk: Quality regressions when soft_token_cap truncates candidates. Mitigation: log examples, add fallback full-run for a small sampled percentage, and surface quality delta metrics to PM/Research.
Risk: Starvation of high-throughput customers due to deadline flush churn. Mitigation: implement tenant-aware scheduling and minimum reserved slot counts per customer tier.
Risk: Increased complexity in debugging failed reranks. Mitigation: enrich trace ids with shard ids and include shard-level timings in traces and logs.
tests_and_benchmarks: Synthetic mixed workload (config files in /infra/perf/rerank/mixed-70-30.yaml) — baseline vs adaptive-shards
Soak test: 24-hour run with production-like traffic on staging cluster to detect OOMs and latency regressions
Quality eval: run existing rerank eval harness (research/rerank-evals) on 1k annotated queries comparing top-10 agreement between baseline and soft-capped runs
Canary rollout plan: 0.5% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics guardrails on P99, error rate, and quality delta
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on shard selection heuristic and the deadline flush invariants. Pay attention to how we surface soft_capped requests for post-hoc quality analysis.
final_notes: If the P99 improvements hold in extended soak tests and OOMs are mitigated by adaptive shard limits, plan to include this behind a runtime flag and enable for 'latency-priority' customer tier in runtime-1.22 rollout.
